historical_record.description: Under the Open Space and Park Renovation Program, the Recreation and Park Commission ratified the acquisition of the Knudsen property on Potrero, between 25th and Army Streets, Lots 10 and 14 of Block 4277.

The Recreation and Park Commission engaged Esherick Hornsey Dodge and Davis, for a $45,000 fee, to program and design a park on Lots 10 and 14 of Block 4277, the Knudsen-Bloom property, with a construction budget of $800,000.

The Recreation and Park Commission ratified a $109,700 agreement with Esherick Hornsey Dodge and Davis, architects, to design and oversee construction of the recreation and park facilities on the Knudsen-Bloom property, at Potrero Avenue near 25th Street.

When the Art Commission, at its Phase III review, disapproved the fence, the grading and an orchard of trees in the design for the Knudsen-Bloom property, halting the work, the Recreation and Park Commission asked the City Attorney whether the Art Commission had any authority over the landscape design at that stage.
The Recreation and Park Commission ratified the award of the contract to develop the Knudsen-Bloom property as a park to Munkdale Brothers, Inc. at $869,320.
